citation.title: Optimisation of three-dimensional hierarchical structures with tailored lattice metamaterial anisotropy
citation.authors: Lei Zhu; Liao Sun; Xiaoyang Wang; Nan Li
citation.version_coded: version of record, Imperial College Spiral repository

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: At volume fraction 0.3, the optimized anisotropic primitive-cubic lattice has 30.6% lower compliance than classical SIMP and 13.0% lower compliance than a quasi-isotropic lattice.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No paired classical and ML runtime figures or factor stated.
claim.alternatives: Abstract reports qualitative structural-efficiency advantage; section 5.2 compares normalized compliance across nine MBB-beam cases, with additional L-shaped and torsion cases.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP density-based topology optimization with penalty p=3 (section 5, Iso-P3)
baseline.implementation: Nastran 2018 optimization module with MATLAB preprocessing; modified method of feasible directions (sections 4-5)
baseline.problem_size: 3D MBB beam, L-shaped beam, and cantilever beam; mesh element count not stated (section 5)
baseline.classical_iterations: relative objective change and constraint violation convergence criteria; numerical thresholds not stated (sections 2.1, 5)
baseline.data_generation_cost: Numerical homogenization on 165 PC, 330 BCC, and 1327 PCBCC sample lattices; wall-clock cost not stated (section 3.1)
baseline.quality_metric: FE-optimized compliance under maximum volume-fraction constraint (sections 5-6)
baseline.quality_gap: MBB beam at volume fraction 0.3: PC-A compliance 30.6% below Iso-P3 and 13.0% below PC-Q (conclusion)

R1.evidence: Conclusion: primary outcome is 30.6% lower compliance at stated volume fraction; no speed comparison.

R2.evidence: Conclusion: primary outcome compares design quality rather than runtime.

R3.evidence: Conclusion: primary outcome compares design quality rather than runtime.

R4.evidence: Sections 4-5: optimized compliance is obtained with Nastran FE analysis and a maximum volume-fraction constraint; detailed-lattice FE validation is sampled in section 5.1. Infeasible or failed-design rates are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: three case studies: MBB beam, L-shaped beam, cantilever torsion (section 5)

notes: The paper uses an ANN surrogate for the forward lattice-property map inside iterative FE optimization, so the learned model contributes to optimization rather than forward analysis alone. The full version of record is available in Imperial College Spiral after the publisher PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403.
